Formal Total Synthesis of (−)-Isolaurallene and Structure
Determination of (+)-4-epi-Isolaurallene via Stereodivergent
Intramolecular Amide Enolate Alkylation

ABSTRACT: Described herein are the formal total syntheses of
(−)-isolaurallene (1) and structure determination of newly isolated
(+)-4-epi-isolaurallene (2) via a highly stereodivergent intra-
molecular amide enolate alkylation (IAEA) strategy. Highly
stereoselective constructions of α,α′-trans-THF 3 and α,α′-cis-
THF 4 were accomplished by subjecting common intermediate 5 to
non-chelate-controlled and chelate-controlled IAEA, respectively.
The former protocol greatly improves the moderate stereo-
selectivity previously observed in constructing α,α′-trans-THF
rings via intramolecular nitrile anion alkylation (INAA).
T
he Laurencia genus of red algae has yielded a plethora of
oxacyclic halogenated C
15
acetogenins, some of which
feature a stereoisomeric dioxabicyclic bromoallene skeleton
comprising the 2,10-dioxabicyclo[7.3.0]dodecene moiety.
1
Among these, the first natural product with this structure
was (−)-isolaurallene (1), which was isolated from the red alga
Laurencia nipponica by Kurata and co-workers in 1982.
2
As
shown in Figure 1, spectroscopic and single-crystal X-ray
crystallographic studies revealed that (−)-isolaurallene (1) is
composed of an α,α′-cis-oxonene unit fused with an α,α′-trans-
THF ring, which is substituted with an (R)-bromoallene
appendage at C(4). The first total synthesis of this natural
product was accomplished by the Crimmins group, who
employed an Evans asymmetric allylation and nine-membered
ether ring-closing metathesis (RCM) to the α,α′-cis-oxonene as
key steps.
3
The α,α′-trans-THF ring in 1 was then constructed
by an asymmetric epoxidation/internal Williamson ether-
ification sequence. Subsequently, our group achieved a total
synthesis of 1 utilizing a stereoselective intermolecular amide
enolate alkylation/RCM strategy for the α,α′-cis-oxonene and
intramolecular nitrile anion alkylation (INAA) for the α,α′-
trans-THF ring.
4
Meanwhile, (+)-4-epi-isolaurallene (2), another closely
related C
15
acetogenin with a 2,10-dioxabicyclo[7.3.0]-
dodecene unit, was recently isolated from a population of
marine red alga Laurencia nangii Masuda by Vairappan and co-
workers in 2020.
5
The structure of (+)-4-epi-isolaurallene was
elucidated from extensive spectroscopic studies. A comparison
of its
1
H NMR spectrum with those of related natural and
unnatural compounds revealed that the 2,10-
dioxabicyclo[7.3.0]dodecene unit comprises an α,α′-cis-oxo-

positive rotation of (+)-4-epi-isolaurallene ([α]
25
D
+56.1 (c
0.46, CHCl
3
)), the absolute stereochemistry of the bromoal-
lene moiety was assigned as S on the basis of Lowe’s rule.
6
However, since the relative stereochemistry between the
dioxabicyclic core and the bromoallene moiety could not be
determined using spectroscopic methods, the structure of
(+)-4-epi-isolaurallene was proposed to be either 2a or 2b
(Figure 1). No total synthesis of this natural product has been
reported to date, and thus, its structure has remained
unconfirmed.
As stated above, we recently reported the stereoselective
substrate-controlled total synthesis of (−)-isolaurallene (1),
which involved the construction of the α,α′-trans-THF moiety
via INAA with a trans:cis selectivity of 5.8:1. In an effort to
improve this modest stereoselectivity, and based on the
insights acquired during our recent total syntheses of other
tetrahydrofuranoid natural products, we envisioned that the
use of KHMDS as the base in the presence of a crown ether
might produce an α,α′-trans-THF in a highly stereoselective
manner, thereby enabling a stereodivergent intramolecular
amide enolate alkylation (IAEA) strategy for the selective
construction of both α,α′-cis and α,α′-trans THF moieties from
a common substrate.
7a
Herein, we describe the formal total synthesis of
(−)-isolaurallene (1) and consequent structure determination
of (+)-4-epi-isolaurallene (2) via the highly stereoselective total
syntheses of ent-2a and 2b employing our highly stereo-
divergent IAEA strategy in a substrate-controlled manner.
As shown in our retrosynthetic plan (Scheme 1), we were
confident that α,α′-trans-THF amide 3 and its C(4) epimer,
α,α′-cis-THF amide 4, could lead to (−)-isolaurallene (1) and
4-epi-isolaurallenes (ent-2a and 2b), respectively, via the RCM
and Overman protocol. It is worth mentioning at this point
that we opted to synthesize ent-2a and 2b instead of the
originally proposed structures 2a and 2b for the sake of
simplicity in our approach to determine the relative stereo-
chemistry between the dioxabicyclic core and the bromoallene
appendage of (+)-4-epi-isolaurallene (2). Moreover, with the
knowledge accrued during the aforementioned recent total
syntheses of natural products containing a THF ring,
7
we
envisaged that pivotal intermediates α,α′-trans-THF 3 and
α,α′-cis-THF 4 could be constructed via non-chelate-
controlled and chelate-controlled IAEA, respectively, in a
stereodivergent fashion from common substrate ω-tosyl α-
alkoxyamide 5, which could be obtained from known
compound 6.
4
Our synthesis commenced with the preparation of stereo-
divergent IAEA substrate 5 as described in Scheme 2. Known
compound 6 was converted into IAEA substrate ω-tosyl α-
alkoxyamide 5 in a good overall yield (66%) via a
straightforward four-step sequence. Thus, chemoselective
deprotection of the MOM group in the presence of the
TIPS group in 6 by treatment with trifluoroacetic acid and
subsequent Williamson etherification of the resulting secon-
dary alcohol 7 with N,N-dimethyl chloroacetamide furnished
α-alkoxyamide 8. Removal of the TIPS protecting group in 8
with TBAF followed by tosylation of the resultant primary
alcohol with p-toluenesulfonic anhydride delivered the desired
internal alkylation substrate 5.
With ω-tosyl α-alkoxyamide 5 in hand, we proceeded to
implement the pivotal stereodivergent IAEA reaction in the
construction of both α,α′-trans-THF 3 and α,α′-cis-THF 4, as
depicted in Scheme 3. As anticipated, treatment of 5 with
LiHMDS in toluene at −78 to −50 °C for 3 h furnished the
desired α,α′-cis-THF amide 4 in excellent yield (93%) and
diastereoselectivity (47:1 cis:trans, by
1
H NMR analysis),

In conclusion, we accomplished the highly stereoselective
construction of α,α′-trans-THF 3 and α,α′-cis-THF 4 from a
common cyclization substrate 5 using a highly stereodivergent
IAEA reaction in a non-chelate-controlled and chelate-
controlled manner, respectively. Our non-chelate-controlled
IAEA protocol markedly improved upon the moderate
stereoselectivity previously observed in the construction of
the α,α′-trans-THF ring via INAA (trans only via IAEA vs
5.8:1 trans:cis via INAA). By applying this methodology, the
formal total synthesis of (−)-isolaurallene (1) was achieved
and the structure of (+)-4-epi-isolaurallene (2) was confirmed
unambiguously to be 2a via the total synthesis of its
enantiomer (ent-2a). Furthermore, our stereodivergent IAEA
protocol could be applicable to stereoselective syntheses of 2,5-
cis- and 2,5-trans-3-hydroxy tetrahydrofuranoid natural prod-
ucts, in particular, dioxabicyclic bromoallene Laurencia marine
natural products with a 2,10-dioxabicyclo[7.3.0]dodecane.

In conclusion, we accomplished the highly stereoselective
construction of α,α′-trans-THF 3 and α,α′-cis-THF 4 from a
common cyclization substrate 5 using a highly stereodivergent
IAEA reaction in a non-chelate-controlled and chelate-
controlled manner, respectively. Our non-chelate-controlled
IAEA protocol markedly improved upon the moderate
stereoselectivity previously observed in the construction of
the
\alpha , \alpha ^ { \prime } .
-trans-THF ring via INAA (trans only via IAEA vs
5.8:1 trans:cis via INAA). By applying this methodology, the
formal total synthesis of (−)-isolaurallene (1) was achieved
and the structure of (+)-4-epi-isolaurallene (2) was confirmed
unambiguously to be 2a via the total synthesis of its
enantiomer (ent-2a). Furthermore, our stereodivergent IAEA
protocol could be applicable to stereoselective syntheses of
2 , 5 \mathrm { - }
cis- and 2,5-trans-3-hydroxy tetrahydrofuranoid natural prod-
ucts, in particular, dioxabicyclic bromoallene Laurencia marine
natural products with a 2,10-dioxabicyclo[7.3.0]dodecane.
